title: Elon Musk: SpaceX Could Be Worth Vastly More Than Earth's Economy
summary:
"This will sound super crazy, but I see a path to SpaceX being worth orders of magnitude more than the current Earth economy," the Tesla and SpaceX CEO wrote in a Thursday post on X.
SpaceX had a $2.2 trillion market capitalization at Thursday's close, meaning the global economy is worth roughly 57 times more.

title: British Airways is launching the world's largest business-class cabin on its Airbus A380s. Take a look inside.
summary:
Airlines love business class, and British Airways' latest updates to its Airbus A380s are proof.
This week, the airline unveiled a major overhaul to the interiors of its superjumbos, including what it says is the world's largest business-class cabin, with over 100 suites spanning the double-decker jet's upper floor.
Over 35,000 individual parts are installed on each aircraft as part of the retrofit, which includes new galleys and staircases, British Airways said.
While the A380 has fallen out of favor with many airlines since the pandemic, it still plays a key role in British Airways' fleet.
The flag carrier has 12 such airplanes — the second most behind Emirates.

title: 'SNL' takes aim at Kevin O’Leary and his Utah data center: 'I'm going to make the future go away’
summary:
AI data centers got the "Weekend Update" treatment on "Saturday Night Live" this week.
The "SNL" version of O'Leary said he understood that some Americans were concerned about data centers near their homes.
(An actual May Gallup poll found that over half of American surveyors opposed constructing AI data centers in their local area.)
Leading tech companies rely on AI data centers to power their systems and products.
Add to Preferred SourcesO'Leary scaled back the data center's size from about 40,000 to just over 20,000 acres after public pushback.

title: Vittorio Colao defends copyright rules and the DSA in Europe’s AI debate
summary:
Regulation is holding back AI in Europe, but not every rule in the same way, Vittorio Colao said.
Intellectual property and the value of creative work need protecting, he said.
“So when AI companies complain about copyright laws, I say, you see, sorry guys, you want me to allow stealing?” Colao said.
“Good intentions, too complicated to implement, and now we are not capable of implementing it,” Colao said of the AI Act.
Four risks to work onBeyond the debate over extinction, Colao named four AI risks: jobs and social impact, people’s judgement, wealth concentration and cybersecurity.

title: Trump’s AI liability push leaves rogue-agent blame unclear, Bloomberg says
summary:
But it is far from clear who would pay when an AI agent goes rogue, Maggie Eastland reported for Bloomberg.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and former White House AI czar David Sacks argue that existing liability laws work better than new rules.
A warning from the SI ForceLate on Friday, the White House’s new Super Intelligence Force told AI firms to report incidents with their models and fix any harm.
The main US hacking law requires proof of intent, which is hard to pin on an AI agent acting on its own.
It is also unclear whether the blame lies with the company that built a model or the business that used it.

title: King Charles warns malicious online actors are evolving their tactics
summary:
King Charles III has warned of the challenges disinformation and other "hostile online activity" pose to trust and security in the digital age.
The comments, made in a letter to the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to mark its 10th anniversary, spoke of "malicious actors" continuing to "evolve their tactics by using automated technologies".
"From threats to our international order, to the need to balance the risks and opportunities of powerful new technologies, strong cyber security is fundamental to making the online environment safer and more resilient," he wrote.
Last month, the King warned AI executives of the "existential dangers" posed by the technology falling into the wrong hands.
In the letter published on Saturday by NCSC, the King praised the government agency.

title: Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’
summary:
He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.
In a lengthy post on X, Microsoft’s CEO laid out his views on the dangers posed by highly advanced AI models and how to confront those risks.
Nadella says we can no longer accept a world where AI is treated as a “set of nested black boxes” whose advice and actions we simply accept or reject.
More advanced models will require more advanced containment technologies that we need to standardize on.
Unfortunately, Nadella also refers to AI as “super intelligence” throughout the post.

title: Satya Nadella says a company's relationship with AI should have trust issues
summary:
Satya Nadella says that in the relationship between AI and a company, trust issues can be healthy.
Nadella said that AI models aren't inherently malicious, but anything with access to vital systems can become compromised or make mistakes.
Add to Preferred SourcesAs the pace of AI development continues to pick up, everyone is clamoring for stricter guardrails, including the companies building the AI models themselves.
Nadella's remarks come after a series of cybersecurity incidents rocked the AI industry.
Nadella also said companies need to disclose when their AI systems fail or become compromised to the affected parties in a timely manner.

title: My friends use AI regularly, but I refuse to. I'm learning to keep my beliefs and opinions about it to myself.
summary:
My reaction to using AI to design my next lesson plan was not positive.
I do realize that I cannot entirely resist technological change, but choosing to do my own thing instead of using AI is my choice right now.
What makes me most uncomfortable is feeling like I'm being interrogated about why I'm choosing not to use it.
Whether or not I'm using AI in my day-to-day life is irrelevant to our friendship unless she asks for my direct opinion on it.
I'm still pretty resistant to the technology, but I'm even more resistant to making anyone who uses it feel bad about it.

title: DistroKid has been quietly taking down songs in response to UMG lawsuit
summary:
Artists are taking to social media to complain that DistroKid has unceremoniously removed their work without notice.
Now DistroKid has confirmed to The Verge that the takedowns are a direct response to claims made by UMG.
Musician and self-described “Video Game boy” McGwire reported that six of his songs had been removed from streaming.
Most infuriating for McGwire was a song removed for an uncleared sample.
He told The Verge that an entire album for an artist he had been working with was removed with no communication or explanation.

title: AI is creating a 'human premium' for art created by people
summary:
But here's a third statistic: more than half of those surveyed said they did care if it was made by AI.
Daniel Susskind, an economics professor at King's College London, says many of us place huge value on the human role in making art.
It's what makes the creative process different from more functional, practical tasks, he thinks.
"I was once in a room of accountants, and one of them stood up and said, 'My clients come to me for the personal touch, the human process'," he remembers.
As Susskind describes it, what we value isn't just the destination, it's the knowledge that a human - one of us - got us there.

title: Google's Open-Source Bug Bounty Program Has A Big AI Problem
summary:
Bug bounty programs are intended to be mutually beneficial: Major organizations get to plug holes in their security while hackers skilled enough to find vulnerabilities are paid for their effort.
These were among the highest-paying bounty programs, meaning ethical hackers now have fewer ways to profit from their talents.
Google previously awarded up to $31,337 for the most serious reported vulnerabilities with Intel going as high as $150,000.
In the meantime, bounty hunters are encouraged to continue submitting reports to Google's other VRP or Patch Rewards programs, which remain active.
Alternatively, you could try claiming Apple's $2 million bounty for discovering exploits that can achieve the same goals as a sophisticated mercenary spyware attack.

title: UK can’t rely on AI that could be switched off, Turing chief tells Guardian
summary:
The UK must not depend on foreign AI that could be cut off at short notice, the new head of the Alan Turing Institute has said.
“We shouldn’t depend solely on systems we can’t inspect or control, or that could be restricted or even switched off,” Williamson said.
He pointed to defence, national security, critical infrastructure and healthcare as areas where AI is now built in.
Williamson said the UK should have some AI it does not need anyone’s permission to use.
The institute cannot match the budgets of big AI labs, he added, but it could build smaller, nationally owned models for start-ups.
